=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
  Line or code reference: 1549-1552 and 1558
  Problem: Pre-existing cached cancelled rows are reused by the `run_id in jobs_seen_lookup` fast path even though they predate this change and still contain a null `failure_point`; the new cancelled job-fetch branch at line 1558 is never reached for them.
  Why it fails at runtime: On the first collector run after deployment, a cancelled run already present in the ai-memory `rows_snapshot` was recorded under the old code via the `elif run_id > 0` branch, so its `run_id` is in `jobs_seen_lookup`. The loop executes the `continue` at lines 1551-1553 and emits the stale null `failure_point`, leaving the run locationless until it ages out of the cache or the cache is cleared.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 944-945 and 1002-1005
  Problem: When the Python audit exits non-zero before `_emit_coverage_summary` runs, `_write_summary` still writes the initialized `coverage_status="full"`, `logs_fetched=0`, and `logs_missing=0` values. The step-summary coverage block is gated only on `da_summary_loaded`, not on `da_status != "error"`.
  Why it fails at runtime: On an error run where jq is available, the summary prints `Status: error` alongside `Log coverage: full` and `Log fetches: fetched 0 / missing 0`, falsely claiming full coverage when coverage was never computed.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/summarize_unselected_runs.py
  Line or code reference: 326-333, with eligibility at 193-213
  Problem: The collector now populates `failure_point` for cancelled runs, but this downstream formatter still labels any non-null `failure_point` as `Failing job/step (collector-detected)`.
  Why it fails at runtime: `select_targets` does not exclude cancelled runs, so unselected cancelled runs are fetched and passed to `_format_user_message`. The prompt sent to the summarizer then misclassifies the cancellation as a failure, producing misleading `log_summary` content for workflow-log analysis.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: line 919, `IFS=$'\t' read -r da_status da_coverage_status da_processed_runs da_marker_occurrences da_persistent_clusters da_skipped_absent_path da_logs_fetched da_logs_missing da_missing_run_ids da_created da_edited da_closed da_suppressed`
  Problem: `da_processed_runs` appears twice in the read variable list (positions 3 and 13). Since jq writes exactly 13 tab-separated fields, bash reads 13 values into positions 1–13 of the variable list: `da_processed_runs` at position 3 gets the field-3 value `5`, then `da_processed_runs` at position 13 overwrites it with the field-13 value (the actual suppressed count). `da_suppressed` has no variable and stays at default `0`. The 14th variable (`da_processed_runs` again) is never assigned.
  Why it fails at runtime: In every successful jq parse, `da_processed_runs` is silently overwritten with the wrong metric (suppressed count instead of processed-runs count), and `da_suppressed` is always `0` even when the summary has a real non-zero suppressed count. The Telegram detail, step summary, and GitHub Actions job summary all display wrong or zero values for these two fields.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
  Line or code reference: lines 1581–1582 (jobs_seen_set population for non-failure/cancelled runs that don't match the cache reuse branch)
  Problem: Cancelled runs that were cached before this change (or whose cache entry predates the jobs_seen_set migration) are reused from cached_rows_by_run_id when run_id is already in jobs_seen_lookup, bypassing list_jobs_for_run. Their failure_point stays null because compute_run_metrics sees an empty jobs list.
  Why it fails at runtime: Any cancelled run whose cache row was written before this change (or whose run_id was already recorded in jobs_seen_set before the cancellation metadata was available) is never re-fetched, so its cached failure_point remains {"job_name": None, "step_name": None} indefinitely.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 892–900 (shell variable defaults) and lines 947–960 (display block gated by da_summary_loaded only)
  Problem: When jq is available and the Python block exits non-zero, _write_summary runs first and writes the hard-coded defaults (coverage_status="full", logs_fetched=0, logs_missing=0) to the summary file before the shell reads it. The shell then reads those defaults via jq and da_summary_loaded becomes "true", so the display block renders 0/0/0 as if coverage were fully successful.
  Why it fails at runtime: An erroring audit (e.g. downstream API failure) silently surfaces as "Log coverage: full" and "Log fetches: fetched 0 / missing 0" in the step summary and Telegram alert because the display block is gated only by successful jq parse, not by audit_rc==0.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: all listed issue #3753 requirements were reported satisfied; no task gaps.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
